units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay, we're out of the cab. It's quiet, and the houses are small.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You're on Menomonee Street, in the part of Old Town called the Old Town Triangle.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Look at the houses. Some are small wooden cottages, and some are brick.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Why is it so... cottagey?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Because of a fire. German immigrants settled this area in the 1850s, and community life centered on Saint Michael Church.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Then came the Great Chicago Fire of 1871.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: The big one.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It destroyed all the houses here and most of the church.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: This is a serious part of the story, and it's why the street looks like it does.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Residents rebuilt quickly with small frame worker's-style cottages.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Wood, after a fire?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Yes, and then a city ordinance banned further wood construction.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Later houses were built of brick and stone, and that's the mix you see.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The district includes at least one fire relief cottage.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: A relief cottage. So these are houses made by charity.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The district notes at least one.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Look for a very small, simple wooden house, and imagine how many people needed one.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. I'm looking at it differently now.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Now look at the brick garages with apartments above.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Those were built for the chauffeurs of nearby Gold Coast residents.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: The chauffeurs lived over the garage.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Ha. A tiny apartment above a car.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And the neighborhood almost didn't last.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In the 1940s, community concern led to what's described as one of the nation's earliest neighborhood revitalization efforts, which helped keep these narrow, tree-lined streets and their character.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So some of the people who live here fought to save it.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: They did. Walk slowly. When you're ready, head west toward Sedgwick Street, and the tavern is on the corner.
